newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Crimean parliament elects pro-Russian speaker.
newsitem.headline: Crimean parliament elects pro-Russian speaker.

text.p: The parliament of Ukraine's autonomous Crimean peninsula on Thursday elected a pro-Russian speaker who pledged to restore economic ties with Moscow while remaining politically loyal to Kiev.
In a secret ballot deputies voted 59 to 26 for Vasily Kiselyov, a former collective farm boss, to head parliament in the Crimean region, populated mainly by ethnic Russians.

"The renewal of pro-Russian feeling is possible only in the economic sphere and I'll do everything to restore business ties with Russia," Kiselyov told the chamber after his election. "But I don't accept (pro-Russian) political separatism."
The region, with a population of 2.7 million, was part of Russia for nearly two centuries until the Kremlin gave it to Ukraine, then a Soviet republic, as a "gift" in 1954.
Deputies on Wednesday accepted the resignation of pro-Ukrainian speaker Yevhen Suprunyuk. Four pro-Russian factions had demanded Suprunyuk's resignation, accusing him of being too close to Kiev.
